techniques.name: Active Scanning
techniques.description: Adversary probes victim infrastructure (ports, vulnerabilities) before access.

techniques.name: Gather Victim Host Information
techniques.description: Collecting details about victim hosts (OS, hardware) from open sources.

techniques.name: Gather Victim Identity Information
techniques.description: Harvesting employee names, emails and credentials from public sources.

techniques.name: Phishing for Information
techniques.description: Soliciting information from targets via deceptive messages.

techniques.name: Acquire Infrastructure
techniques.description: Buying or leasing domains, servers or services used to stage operations.

techniques.name: Establish Accounts
techniques.description: Creating social-media or email accounts to support targeting.

techniques.name: Obtain Capabilities
techniques.description: Acquiring tooling, exploits or certificates rather than developing them.

techniques.name: Phishing
techniques.description: Sending deceptive messages to induce execution or credential entry.

techniques.name: Spearphishing Attachment
techniques.description: Targeted email carrying a malicious attachment to be opened by the user.

techniques.name: Spearphishing Link
techniques.description: Targeted email with a link to a credential-harvest or malware page.

techniques.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
techniques.description: Exploiting an internet-exposed application to gain a foothold.

techniques.name: External Remote Services
techniques.description: Using exposed remote services (VPN, RDP gateway, Citrix) to enter.

techniques.name: Valid Accounts
techniques.description: Using legitimate credentials to access systems and blend in.

techniques.name: Valid Accounts: Domain Accounts
techniques.description: Using compromised domain credentials across the environment.

techniques.name: Trusted Relationship
techniques.description: Abusing a trusted third-party or MSP connection to reach the target.

techniques.name: Drive-by Compromise
techniques.description: User's browser is compromised by visiting a malicious or watering-hole site.

techniques.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
techniques.description: Abusing command and script interpreters to run adversary code.

techniques.name: PowerShell
techniques.description: Using PowerShell for execution, often encoded or with download cradles.

techniques.name: Windows Command Shell
techniques.description: Using cmd.exe to run commands, chain tools and batch scripts.

techniques.name: Visual Basic
techniques.description: Executing VBScript/VBA, frequently from Office macros.

techniques.name: Python
techniques.description: Using a Python interpreter to execute cross-platform tooling.

techniques.name: User Execution: Malicious File
techniques.description: User opens a delivered file (document, LNK, ISO) that runs code.

techniques.name: Windows Management Instrumentation
techniques.description: Using WMI to execute commands locally or on remote hosts.

techniques.name: System Services: Service Execution
techniques.description: Running a binary by creating/starting a Windows service.

techniques.name: Native API
techniques.description: Executing via direct OS API calls to avoid spawning command-line tools.

techniques.name: Create Account: Local Account
techniques.description: Creating a local account to retain access to a host.

techniques.name: Account Manipulation
techniques.description: Modifying accounts (group membership, credentials) to keep access.

techniques.name: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
techniques.description: Adding a program to Run keys or the Startup folder for autostart.

techniques.name: Create or Modify System Process: Windows Service
techniques.description: Installing or altering a Windows service for persistence/SYSTEM.

techniques.name: Scheduled Task
techniques.description: Creating a scheduled task that re-launches payloads.

techniques.name: Server Software Component: Web Shell
techniques.description: Planting a web shell on a server for remote command execution.

techniques.name: Hijack Execution Flow: DLL Side-Loading
techniques.description: Placing a malicious DLL next to a signed binary that loads it.

techniques.name: BITS Jobs
techniques.description: Using the BITS service to download and persist payloads stealthily.

techniques.name: WMI Event Subscription
techniques.description: Registering a permanent WMI event consumer to trigger code.

techniques.name: Abuse Elevation Control: Bypass UAC
techniques.description: Bypassing User Account Control to elevate without a prompt.

techniques.name: Access Token Manipulation
techniques.description: Manipulating access tokens to run code in another security context.

techniques.name: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
techniques.description: Exploiting a software/kernel flaw to gain higher privileges.

techniques.name: Process Injection
techniques.description: Injecting code into another process to evade defenses and elevate.

techniques.name: Domain Policy Modification: Group Policy
techniques.description: Altering Group Policy to push privileged changes domain-wide.

techniques.name: Indicator Removal: Clear Windows Event Logs
techniques.description: Clearing event logs to remove traces of activity.

techniques.name: Indicator Removal: File Deletion
techniques.description: Deleting files dropped during the operation.

techniques.name: Obfuscated Files or Information
techniques.description: Encoding or packing files and commands to hinder analysis.

techniques.name: Command Obfuscation
techniques.description: Obscuring command-line content (encoding, concatenation).

techniques.name: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools
techniques.description: Disabling or tampering with security software.

techniques.name: Impair Defenses: Disable Windows Event Logging
techniques.description: Turning off or weakening Windows audit logging.

techniques.name: System Binary Proxy Execution: Rundll32
techniques.description: Using rundll32.exe to proxy execution of code.

techniques.name: System Binary Proxy Execution: Mshta
techniques.description: Using mshta.exe to execute HTA/script content.

techniques.name: Masquerading
techniques.description: Naming/placing tools to look legitimate (e.g. svchost in user path).

techniques.name: Modify Registry
techniques.description: Changing registry keys to evade defenses or hide configuration.

techniques.name: Deobfuscate/Decode Files or Information
techniques.description: Decoding staged payloads on the host (certutil, base64).

techniques.name: OS Credential Dumping: LSASS Memory
techniques.description: Reading LSASS memory to extract credentials.

techniques.name: OS Credential Dumping: SAM
techniques.description: Extracting the local SAM database for password hashes.

techniques.name: OS Credential Dumping: NTDS
techniques.description: Copying NTDS.dit from a domain controller for all domain hashes.

techniques.name: Brute Force: Password Spraying
techniques.description: Trying one/few passwords across many accounts to avoid lockout.

techniques.name: Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets: Kerberoasting
techniques.description: Requesting service tickets to crack SPN account passwords offline.

techniques.name: Credentials from Password Stores
techniques.description: Extracting credentials from browsers, vaults and credential managers.

techniques.name: Unsecured Credentials: Credentials In Files
techniques.description: Searching files/scripts for plaintext credentials.

techniques.name: Input Capture: Keylogging
techniques.description: Recording keystrokes to capture credentials and data.

techniques.name: Account Discovery: Domain Account
techniques.description: Enumerating domain accounts and groups.

techniques.name: System Information Discovery
techniques.description: Collecting host OS, hardware and configuration details.

techniques.name: File and Directory Discovery
techniques.description: Enumerating files and directories of interest.

techniques.name: Remote System Discovery
techniques.description: Discovering other hosts on the network.

techniques.name: Process Discovery
techniques.description: Listing running processes to understand the host.

techniques.name: System Network Configuration Discovery
techniques.description: Enumerating local network configuration and connections.

techniques.name: Network Service Discovery
techniques.description: Scanning for reachable services on internal hosts.

techniques.name: Domain Trust Discovery
techniques.description: Enumerating domain trust relationships for lateral paths.

techniques.name: Permission Groups Discovery: Domain Groups
techniques.description: Enumerating domain groups (e.g. Domain Admins).

techniques.name: Remote Services: RDP
techniques.description: Moving between hosts via Remote Desktop.

techniques.name: Remote Services: SMB/Windows Admin Shares
techniques.description: Using admin shares (C$, ADMIN$) to move and execute.

techniques.name: Remote Services: Windows Remote Management
techniques.description: Using WinRM/PowerShell Remoting to run commands remotely.

techniques.name: Lateral Tool Transfer
techniques.description: Copying tools between hosts inside the network.

techniques.name: Use Alternate Authentication Material: Pass the Hash
techniques.description: Authenticating with a stolen NTLM hash instead of a password.

techniques.name: Exploitation of Remote Services
techniques.description: Exploiting a vulnerable internal service to move laterally.

techniques.name: Data from Local System
techniques.description: Collecting files of interest from a compromised host.

techniques.name: Data from Network Shared Drive
techniques.description: Collecting data from accessible network shares.

techniques.name: Archive Collected Data: Archive via Utility
techniques.description: Compressing/encrypting staged data with an archiver before exfil.

techniques.name: Email Collection
techniques.description: Collecting email content from local or server mailboxes.

techniques.name: Screen Capture
techniques.description: Capturing screenshots of the victim desktop.

techniques.name: Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols
techniques.description: C2 over HTTP/HTTPS blending with normal web traffic.

techniques.name: Application Layer Protocol: DNS
techniques.description: C2 or exfil tunnelled over DNS queries.

techniques.name: Ingress Tool Transfer
techniques.description: Downloading additional tools from external infrastructure.

techniques.name: Protocol Tunneling
techniques.description: Tunnelling traffic within another protocol to bypass controls.

techniques.name: Proxy
techniques.description: Routing C2 through intermediary proxies/relays.

techniques.name: Encrypted Channel
techniques.description: Encrypting C2 traffic to hide its content.

techniques.name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
techniques.description: Sending stolen data out over the existing C2 channel.

techniques.name: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol
techniques.description: Exfiltrating over a protocol different from the C2 channel.

techniques.name: Exfiltration to Cloud Storage
techniques.description: Uploading data to a cloud storage service.

techniques.name: Automated Exfiltration
techniques.description: Automatically transferring collected data on a schedule.

techniques.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
techniques.description: Encrypting data to disrupt operations and demand ransom.

techniques.name: Inhibit System Recovery
techniques.description: Deleting shadow copies/backups to prevent recovery.

techniques.name: Service Stop
techniques.description: Stopping services (databases, security) before encryption.

techniques.name: Data Destruction
techniques.description: Destroying data/files to disrupt availability.

techniques.name: System Shutdown/Reboot
techniques.description: Shutting down or rebooting systems to disrupt or complete impact.
